findings.what_viewer_sees: The big 'DIG STRAIGHT DOWN TO CHINA?' title (140 px, full opacity) disappears in a single frame at 3:56.77 while the globe behind it carries on. It goes exactly as the narrator starts 'If you dig straight down, you'll reach China'. There is no scene change to justify it, so it reads as a botched edit.
findings.evidence: Frames 7097-7102 show the complete headline at full strength and 7103 has none, with no fade frames (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/tile_07097_12x1.jpg). Detector E12 (cut, diff 12.1) is this frame. Scene G ends at cChina = 236.76.
findings.likely_cause: The headline is drawn inside scene G's draw2d (the top-down/antipode globe, t1 = cChina) with tOut = cChina - tm.brings + 1.6. Its 0.35 s fade-out is therefore scheduled for 238.36 s, 1.6 s after the scene that draws it has ended, so the scene boundary truncates it.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch2.js:485-487 (headline inside gscene G, which runs t0: cTop, t1: cChina at ch2.js:459-460)
findings.suggested_fix: Move the headline out of G into its own overlay scene that outlives the cut. After ch2.js:489, add push({ t0: tm.brings - 0.2, t1: cChina + 2.0, layer: 5, draw(ctx, lt, t) { F.headline(ctx, ['DIG','STRAIGHT','DOWN','TO',{ w: 'CHINA?', c: PAL.hero }], W / 2, 200, t - tm.brings, { size: 140, per: (tm.myth - tm.brings - 0.25) / 4, tOut: cChina - tm.brings + 1.6 }); } }); and delete lines 485-487. The title then stays up through 'If you dig straight down, you'll reach' and fades at 238.36 s as intended. Keep the globe dimmed under it (see S3-2).

findings.what_viewer_sees: On the same frame as S3-1, the globe (meant to be one unbroken move into China) jerks backwards and brightens. Asia slides about 34 px east (about 6.5 degrees of rotation, against the slow eastward pan it was doing) and the whole globe brightens noticeably. Together with the vanishing title it reads as a jump cut.
findings.evidence: Full-res crops at 7101/7102/7103 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/tile_07101_3x1.jpg). India and Sri Lanka move about 3 px from 7101 to 7102 but about 34 px from 7102 to 7103, and 7103 is clearly brighter. Evaluating the code: scene G at f7102 has lat 29.96, lon 94.49, dim 0.32; scene H at f7103 has lat 30, lon 88, dim 0.
findings.likely_cause: The G to H hand-off parameters do not match at cChina. G's lon is lerp(10,8,k) + 80*k2 + (t - cTop)*0.4: it includes a 0.4 deg/s drift (about 7.1 deg by cChina) and k2 is still 0.994 at the cut. H's first camera key is lon 88. G's look adds 0.2 dim for the headline (dim 0.32), while H's dim is 0 until tm.china - 0.25.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch2.js:463-465 and 468 (scene G k2, camera lon, look dim) vs ch2.js:501 and 506 (scene H keys[0] and look)
findings.suggested_fix: Make H start exactly where G ends. (1) At ch2.js:463, end k2 at the cut: prog(t, tm.brings - 0.6, cChina, E.inOutSine). G then finishes at lat 30, lon 88 + 0.4*(cChina - cTop) (about 95.1). (2) At ch2.js:501, change keys[0] to { t: 0, lat: 30, lon: 88 + 0.4 * (cChina - cTop), alt: 3.0 }. (3) At ch2.js:506, carry the dim over and ease it: dim: lerp(0.32, 0.22, prog(t, cChina + 1.6, tm.china + 0.2)). This keeps the (moved) headline readable and removes the brightness pop.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'Drag the Arctic Ocean down onto Antarctica', the globe holds still for 3 frames while the cyan shape slides, then lurches into a fast spin from standstill (about 5-6 deg/frame, Africa rising about 45 px/frame) and later stops dead. The return on 'But here's the part that doesn't make sense' is worse: the globe holds, then snaps into a ~130 deg whip in only 0.63 s (peak about 9 deg/frame) and stops dead on the Arctic. The surface is unreadable and the start/stop jolts look mechanical.
findings.evidence: Tiles (exact frame numbers) /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/tile_06235_8x1.jpg (globe static 6235-6238, rotating from 6239), tile_06270_8x1.jpg, and tile_06420_30x1.jpg (static 6420-6424, whip 6425-6443, static from 6444). Re-evaluating dragState() and the camera per frame in Python: camera latitude speed goes 0 to 154 deg/s at f6239 and 54 to 0 deg/s at f6274. On the return it goes 0 to 193 deg/s at f6425, peaks at 278 deg/s at f6432, and drops 128 to 0 deg/s at f6443-6444. Detector E9 (3:27.87) is the shape's own full-speed start (E.out).
findings.likely_cause: The camera latitude is the dragged centroid's latitude, hard-clamped: camLat = clamp(la - 6, -64, 66). The centroid moves at up to ~200 deg/s: the forward drag uses E.out, which starts at full speed, and the return is a 1.7 s E.inOut over 172 deg. So the camera sits on a clamp limit, takes on full centroid speed the frame the clamp releases, and loses it the frame it re-clamps. The whole 130 deg return happens in the 0.63 s the centroid spends between the limits.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch2.js:417 (camLat hard clamp); ch2.js:407 (E.out forward drag, 1.7 s E.inOut return); ch2.js:410 (linear, un-eased R2 unwind at tBack)
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Replace the hard clamp at ch2.js:417 with a soft clamp that eases into the limits (C1-continuous, so no velocity jump): const soft = (x, lo, hi, w = 15) => x > hi - w ? hi - w * Math.exp(-(x - hi + w) / w) : x < lo + w ? lo + w * Math.exp((x - lo - w) / w) : x; const camLat = soft(la - 6, -64, 66); (2) Ease the motion itself at ch2.js:407: use E.inOutSine for the forward drag, and lengthen the return: k -= prog(t, tBack, tBack + 2.0, E.inOutSine). Match the alt 'back' ramp at ch2.js:418, and ease the R2 unwind at ch2.js:410 with E.inOut. Peak camera speed falls from about 9 to about 4.5 deg/frame, with no dead starts or stops.

findings.what_viewer_sees: When the Explorer pops out in the Indian Ocean he starts a mid-air somersault but never finishes it. He goes in head-first, and a single boot sticks out of the water like a black post for about 0.2 s. Within about 4 frames he is suddenly upright and waist-deep, with a hand and his head popping out at odd places during the switch. He appears to teleport from feet-up to head-up.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame tiles in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/: tile_07518_24x1.jpg and tile_07542_24x1.jpg show the forward roll in the air ending inverted (7530-7541), head-first entry (7542-7546), only the boot visible (7547-7552), and the upright pose blending in and rising (7553-7557). Close-up: tile_07544_16x1.jpg. Clip lengths read from models/adventurer.glb: Roll = 1.333 s.
findings.likely_cause: ch2.js:168 starts 'Roll' (1.333 s, once) at tm.indian + 0.18 but cross-fades to 'Idle' at tm.indian + 0.95 with a 0.3 s fade. The clip is abandoned at 58%, mid-roll and upside down, so the skeletal crossfade has to turn the body about 180 deg in 0.3 s. Meanwhile the pop curve in bobScene drops him from y=0.3 to -0.47 between u=0.32 and 0.85 s, so the inverted body enters the water head-first.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch2.js:168 (heroP Roll/Idle cues); ch2.js:574 (pop height curve in bobScene)
findings.suggested_fix: Let the roll complete while he is still above water. At ch2.js:168 use .play(tm.indian + 0.02, 'Roll', { fade: 0.06, once: true, speed: 2 }).play(tm.indian + 0.66, 'Idle', { fade: 0.15 }). The roll then ends at u of about 0.75, when y is still about -0.1 on the current curve. Alternatively, swap 'Roll' for a non-inverting reaction such as 'HitRecieve' or 'Wave' so the crossfade never has to flip the body. If a full-speed roll is wanted, keep y >= 0.2 at ch2.js:574 until the clip ends and move the Idle cue to the clip's end.

findings.evidence: Full-res bottom strip /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/tile_05720_4x1.jpg. Frame 5721 shows rock and the whole pill. Frame 5722 shows a navy band from y of about 844 to 1080 cutting through the pill, while the panel has moved only about 1.5 px. Panel offset per the inOutExpo easing (190.70-191.20 s) at frames 5722-5727 is about 1.5, 3.5, 9, 22, 56, 142 px. Detector E4 (motion start at 5722) and E5's pop at (0.66, 0.72) are this band.
findings.likely_cause: drawSouth fills its sky from local y = -300, but the two panels are only 1.05*H apart, so the South backdrop reaches 246 px into the Arctic panel. While wk = 0 the South panel is not drawn (the 'if (wk > 0)' guard). On the first whip frame wk = 0.0012, and the overlapping backdrop appears at full opacity before either panel has visibly moved.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch2.js:271 (ctx.fillRect(0, -300, W, ySLB + 300)); ch2.js:298 (panel spacing H*1.05); ch2.js:319
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the South backdrop to its own panel plus the 54 px gap. At ch2.js:271 use ctx.fillRect(0, -0.05 * H - 4, W, ySLB + 0.05 * H + 4). The Arctic rock (drawn down to H+300) then fills the frame until the South panel actually scrolls in; nothing else in drawSouth reaches above local y=0. Alternatively, increase the panel spacing at ch2.js:298 to H*1.05 + 300.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Just before 'United States', a cyan US shape appears in one frame at full opacity, cut off at the top-left frame edge, while everything else on the map eases. The zoom-out then reveals it.
findings.evidence: Frame 7881 has nothing there; 7882 has the full cyan fill and white outline of the eastern US in the top-left corner (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/tile_07878_24x1.jpg). This is detector E19 (pop at 0.03, 0.17).
findings.likely_cause: The US layer is gated on t > tFlipUS0 - 0.6, and its globalAlpha is usA = 1 - prog(t, tm.start - 0.6, ...), which is already 1. So it has no fade-in, and it starts while the view is still zoomed on the Indian Ocean (the zoom-out begins at tm.us - 0.5 = 262.92).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fade-in: const usIn = prog(t, tFlipUS0 - 0.6, tFlipUS0 - 0.2); then use usA * usIn wherever usA sets globalAlpha in lines 655-657 (fill 0.55*usA*usIn, stroke usA*usIn). Alternatively, gate the layer at tm.us - 0.5 so it arrives with the zoom-out.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The South Pole elevation readout is white text drawn inside the white ice sheet, so '1.8 MI' is only legible through its drop shadow. While it counts up it also under-reports: it starts at '0.0' beside a ruler that is already about 0.4 mi long.
findings.evidence: Full-res frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s3/f_05930.jpg shows '1.8 MI' white on #f4f9ff ice. Frames 5815-5827 in tile_05804_24x1.jpg show '0.0' and '0.1' beside a visible ruler. Per the code, iceTopB(960, kk=0.12) is about 0.40 mi when the count starts.
findings.likely_cause: L.miles is placed at top + 50 (50 px below the ice surface, so on the ice) and shows 1.76*uk. The ruler, however, spans ySLB to top = iceTopB(960, kk), with kk starting at 0.12.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the readout on the dark sky and show the ruler's real length: L.miles(ctx, (ySLB - top) / MI, 1060, top - 34, { size: 54, alpha: prog(t, tm.up - 0.1, tm.up + 0.1) }). Alternatively, give L.miles a dark backing plate when it is drawn over ice.

findings.likely_cause: ovAlpha, and the matching dim term, use env(t, tm.avoid - 0.35, tm.avoid + 1.55, 0.3, 0.45): a fixed 1.9 s window anchored on 'ocean' instead of on the end of the sentence.

Keep the dim continuous with the headline dim: dim: 0.12 + Math.max(0.18 * env(...same window...), 0.2 * prog(t, tm.brings - 0.3, tm.brings + 0.3)). A small two-swatch key (cyan / yellow) would make it readable in the time available.

result.intended_notes:
Frame numbering: tools/grab.py repeats its first decoded frame (ffmpeg's default constant-frame-rate output with the image2 muxer), so every label after the first is one frame too high. In a raw tile the ch1->ch2 cut shows at label 5261 instead of 5260. I used a copy with '-fps_mode passthrough' (review6/s3work/g3.py), so all frame numbers above are exact. The video packet timestamps are continuous from 5260 to 8036: no dropped or duplicate frames.

Intended, reads well:
- 12 of the 13 detector cut events are designed hard cuts landing on narration words: E1 (chapter-2 open, 5260), E2 (5427, on "Santa's"), E3 (cut at 5603, on "two"), E6 (5955, 's027' start), E8 (6167), E10 (6476, on "don't"), E11 (6572, on "Antarctica"), E14 (7348, on "dig"), E15 (7417), E16 (7520), E17 (7577), E18 (7740, on "Not China").
- E5's cut/motion-stop cluster at 3:10.9-3:11.2 is the designed 0.5 s inOutExpo vertical whip with streaks. Only the backdrop band at its head is a defect (S3-5); E4's motion start is that band.
- E6's pops are the designed outBack pop-in of the polar discs. The first frame (5955) is intentionally empty.
- E7 is the designed shutter flash plus negative crossfade on "photographic" (35% white, decaying over 0.3 s).
- E9 is the drag shape's deliberate full-speed start on "Drag". Its camera consequence is S3-3.
- E13 is the designed whip to Kansas: E.in then E.out, with matched speed of about 300 deg/s at the junction, plus streaks.

Defects among the events: E12 (S3-1 and S3-2) and E19 (S3-6). E4 and E5's pop are S3-5.

Chunk seams 5400, 5850, 6300, 6750, 7200 and 7650: the 450k-1 vs 450k pairs were compared numerically. Seam differences equal their neighbours and the mean RGB is continuous, so there is no look change; I found no instance of the tetra-style run-time material toggle in this segment's sets.

Clean at full frame rate:
- Chapter card and Arctic fly-in, NORTH POLE pill, Arctic outline draw.
- Floe gag: wave, Interact and Idle blends are smooth; feet stay planted; cabin floe drift.
- Arctic ruler count and hero reaction.
- South Pole pill, label swap and ice growth: motion fine; only the label legibility issue in S3-7.
- Disc move and headline, negative-to-positive revert.
- Cutaway drill on "line" (fast punch, designed).
- Top-down mirrored outline, yellow fill and pull-back.
- China fill, whip, Kansas pill and push-in.
- Dig gag: the beam reads as held in his hanging hand; the planet correctly occludes him as he sinks.
- Kansas drill cutaway with rider.
- Island line, dot pop and pill swap (2-frame gap).
- Flat map: zoom, equator flash, US card-flip (edge-on at mid-flip, designed), ZERO OVERLAP pill and FALSE stamp slam (legible on its dark plate).
- Narration sync is within 0.4 s everywhere in the segment.

Audio flags, outside visual scope:
- SFX masking at 3:37.65-3:38.00 is likely sfx(tm.line - 0.03, 'impact_deep', -6) at ch2.js:456. It is the loudest ch2 cue (others are -10 to -20 dB) and sits on "line up"; about -14 dB is suggested.
- The voice-tail cuts at 3:05.50 and 4:17.38 come from the narration audio edit, not from ch2 code.
